newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Kabul defenders vow to fight rebel push to death.
newsitem.headline: Kabul defenders vow to fight rebel push to death.

text.p: The Afghan government vowed on Thursday that its forces would fight to the death to defend Kabul as it deployed fresh troops to hold off the rebel Taleban Islamic militia pushing to take the besieged capital.

"We are establishing defences in every street of Kabul," a defence ministry spokesman told reporters as the two sides fought on around the city, ignoring a U.N. Security Council call for an immediate ceasefire and peace talks.
"We have thousands of volunteers from the city," spokesman Amrullah said.
"We are not short of ammunition, fuel, morale or motive. We will remain in Kabul whether we are on the earth or beneath it."
Amrullah said the Taleban had lost hundreds of men to reach the eastern outskirts of Pul-i-Charkhi "and will perhaps lose thousands in Kabul".

A Taleban source in the northwest Pakistani town of Peshawar earlier said the militia forces had penetrated eastern Kabul overnight and were only about five km (three miles) from the presidential palace.

Kabul city itself was calm, and shops and markets were open with no visible sign of panic. But hundreds of people were leaving the city on the road north towards Mazar-i-Sharif in trucks and buses packed with belongings on roofs.
"The Taleban are coming, one hundred percent," an Afghan aid worker said.

"They (government fighters) set up a machine-gun in my street so I thought I had better leave," said Jeff Arnold, programme officer of the German Agro-Action relief agency. "I hope this will all be over quickly so we can come back."
Taleban sources in Pakistan said the militia had further advanced from the south into the shattered city, taken Pul-i-Charkhi and the nearby military academy and Bagrami district in the southeast.
Amrullah said the academy was still with the government, although the Taleban were "very close to us".

Calling the defence of Kabul "a war of identity", Amrullah accused Pakistan of sending military technicians to help the Taleban and said other countries, which he refused to name, were also aiding the rebels.
"We are defending the country's pride against Pakistani puppets. Pakistan wants to control our country. We are ready to give as much sacrifice as required. We don't mind if we die."
But Pakistan denied the accusations.
"We have had and will continue to observe total neutrality while we must maintain a close watch on the events as they develop," a Pakistan Foreign Ministry spokesman said in Islamabad.
The 15-nation U.N. Security Council appealed for a ceasefire and peace talks after a meeting in New York on Wednesday.
Amrullah criticised the United Nations for what he said was inaction when Kabul was on the verge of a catastrophe.
"They know there could be a massacre in Kabul and massive violation of so-called human rights, but they are just watching," he said.
"Kabul is everything. It's the capital. It's the symbol of Afghan identity and we will defend it."
Iranian state radio later on Thursday called for urgent international action to avoid a humanitarian tragedy in Afghanistan.

"World bodies, including the United Nations Security Council, have expressed concern over the situation in Afghanistan... but the Afghan situation is beyond expressions of concern and requires urgent and serious action," Tehran radio said.
Earlier, Defence Ministry sources said government forces had held off overnight Taleban attacks from southeast and southwest of the capital and had deployed fresh troops on all frontlines.
The Taleban attacks came from Butkhak, about 20 km (12 miles) southeast of Kabul, and Koh-i-Koruk, about 20 km to the southwest, they said.
More than 150 rebel fighters were killed in a four-hour battle for a customs house in eastern Kabul starting at midnight, the sources said.

They said the customs house was now no-man's land, but government forces held nearby Pul-i-Charkhi jail, which Taleban sources said the militia had captured. There were government air raids in Pul-i-Charkhi village on Wednesday evening.

The Defence Ministry sources denied a Taleban claim that the militia had advanced up the Tagab valley near the main government airbase of Bagram, north of Kabul, and said the area was firmly in government control.
Government fighters packed on tanks and armoured personnel carriers headed towards the frontlines, witnesses said.

At least 20 foreign aid workers were evacuated from Bagram on two flights arranged by the International Committee of the Red Cross on Thursday as Afghan passengers were preparing to board a flight of the state airline Ariana to India.
Five Ariana planes were parked at Bagram airport along with several MI-8 helicopter gunships and MiG fighters.
